**Subject: Executive Briefing Proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation Summary**

The Profile Block describes Tamarack Instruments as a designer and manufacturer of laboratory measurement instruments, operating in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It records three AI use cases: a deployed customer service chatbot on the support portal, an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Profile Block also records the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers, an internal audit finding of June 2026 noting no inventory of AI systems and ISO/IEC 42001 as a certification target, with work to start next year.

**What the Briefing Covers for the Client**

The Briefing will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to expectations relevant to each listed use case. These include transparency questions for the chatbot and risk classification questions for visual inspection. All are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States developments will appear only as a general landscape item, not as a Client driver.

We will outline what an AI system inventory involves. We will explore how AI governance might connect with the incumbent frameworks listed: ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and internal audit function. The operating model discussion draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen), with board-layer material from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

The stated constraints will frame the discussion: customer data staying in the EU and German works council consultation before anything touches production staff. The session closes with implementation priorities sequenced against Q2 2027, guided by Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human. The Briefing does not provide certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Logistics and Price**

The Briefing is two hours, live virtual, for executive leadership and board-level attendees. Audience roles listed are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The price is US$3,000.

**What the Client Receives Afterward**

The Client receives a written follow-up summary of decisions surfaced, readiness observations and prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a possible next program option.

**Next Step**

We propose confirming the following at intake:

1. Which individuals will attend.
2. Whether the visual inspection pilot affects production staff in a way that requires works council consultation.
3. Whether the chatbot processes personal data.
4. Preferred session dates.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026, and we will propose dates accordingly.

Kind regards,

Senior AI Governance Consultant
AI Governance Academy
